design: Four questions: (1) find rentable assets, (2) validate organic-v1.1 vs Dimension A, (3) test zero-volume community demand, (4) test STANDALONE hyperlocal vs REGIONAL HUB architecture on matched pairs.

models.note: Both rankability models are carried separately on every asset. Neither is overwritten and neither is assumed correct; Wave 1 is the arbiter.

selectionStandards.groupA: measured demand >= 100/mo AND F >= 50 AND organic-v1.1 >= 55 AND geography verified; max 3/service, 2/city
selectionStandards.groupB: community assets are NOT gated on measured volume (that is the hypothesis); admitted on community scale, buildout, affluence, organic-v1.1 and domain availability; matched into pairs then split across architectures
selectionStandards.groupC: selected for information value, explicitly labelled EXPERIMENTAL and never counted as investment-grade

matchedPairs.basis: both VIRGIN, active-buildout, organic 82 vs 79 (Δ3) — the two strongest virgin communities
both VIRGIN, active-buildout, organic 66 vs 67 (Δ1) and 1,400 vs 1,300 homes — the tightest match in the experiment
both VIRGIN, both in McKinney (parent city and its SERP held constant), both large (3,400 vs 7,000 homes), organic 73 vs 63
both INCUMBENT-TARGETED, active-buildout, organic 67 vs 73 (Δ6), 3,000 vs 2,000 homes
both INCUMBENT-TARGETED, organic 65 vs 64 (Δ1) — the tightest incumbent match

unknown: deployment engine per-asset cost (engine not built)
pool content is photo-heavy and likely exceeds the generic content estimate

assets.contentDirective: SERP-derived, not a fixed word count: this is a commercial service query, so the deployment engine should build a commercial service/location experience benchmarked against the observed content bar, not a long informational article.
assets.reasonIncluded: Meets the full pre-stated standard: 260/mo measured demand, F=51 (rentable, ~$576/lead), organic-v1.1 67, geography verified.
assets.hypothesis: An asset with real economics AND a beatable organic SERP should rank and rent. A=91 vs organic=67; where they disagree this asset also contributes model-validation evidence.
assets.successCondition: top-10 organic for the primary query within 6 months AND >=1 inbound lead within 9 months.
assets.failureCondition: no top-20 within 6 months, OR top-10 with zero leads after 3 further months (which falsifies demand, not rankability).

localPackEvidence.note: map pack inherited from the parent city; Google renders no distinct community pack, so this asset must win ORGANIC

assets.contentDirective: Identical specification across BOTH treatments: same visual quality, conversion architecture, topical coverage, schema, publishing window, indexing workflow and tracking. Only the architecture differs.
assets.evidenceConfidence: community class — organic-v1.1 only; no measured demand by construction
assets.geographyVerdict: community within verified metro (SERP localized to parent city)
assets.reasonIncluded: Matched-pair NTX-P1 (both VIRGIN, active-buildout, organic 82 vs 79 (Δ3) — the two strongest virgin communities). Assigned to STANDALONE so the architecture, not the community, is the variable.
assets.hypothesis: Keyword tools report zero volume for "pool builder Sutton Fields", yet homeowners in a 1500-home affluent community may search by community name. A dedicated hyperlocal domain should maximise exact-match relevance. Paired against Legacy Gardens on the hub to isolate architecture.
assets.successCondition: >=100 impressions/month on community-modified queries within 6 months, OR >=1 qualified lead. Architecture comparison is judged on WITHIN-PAIR difference in time-to-first-impression, time-to-top-20 and impressions at 6 months.
assets.failureCondition: indexed but <20 impressions/month after 6 months across ALL community-modified queries while city controls perform in line with measured volume — falsifies hyper-local under-measurement. Architecture verdict is void if fewer than 4 of 6 pairs produce interpretable data.
